articles.title: Venutieri wins it. Now the Reds need another quarterback.
articles.dek: Mt. Silver survived nine sacks and Saffron’s comeback to win 36–33. Tic Thorpe’s six-week injury changes the conversation before the trip to Cinnabar.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Adam Venutieri had already made four field goals when Mt. Silver asked him for the fifth. Saffron had erased a twenty-point halftime deficit, tied the game with seventy-five seconds remaining and given its traveling supporters a reason to believe an extraordinary afternoon might end with something even better. Venutieri’s thirty-three-yard kick, recorded with five seconds left, gave the Reds a 36–33 victory and brought that comeback to a painful stop.

The winning possession belonged to Crem Ftzpatrik. The quarterback completed consecutive seventeen-yard throws to Gregar Jenings after finding Tony Gyarzalez for eight. Garshawn Lynch then ran for nine, and the Reds arranged the final kick. Ftzpatrik finished five of eight for sixty-nine yards and a touchdown. He had entered a game in which NeMarcus Tare seemed determined to meet every passer Mt. Silver could introduce.

Tic Thorpe’s injury report now lists six weeks. Josh Alakazam already has seven remaining on his report. The Reds improved to 13–1 while losing the quarterback who had thrown for 244 yards and two touchdowns that afternoon. Their next opponent, Cinnabar, has just beaten Blackthorn. There will be time to appreciate the winning drive, but Connor McLarren’s preparation has acquired an urgent additional subject.

“Crem got us down there, Adam put it through, and nobody asked whether the afternoon had been convenient,” McLarren said. “We’ll take the win. We’ll also take a good long look at the protection. Nine sacks is a fairly persuasive suggestion.”
Saffron kept reaching the passer

Tare received credit for seven sacks and fourteen pressures. Demedicus Ware added two sacks and seven pressures. Thorpe took seven of the nine sacks charged to Mt. Silver’s quarterbacks; Ftzpatrik took the other two. Those figures explain why a game the Reds led 23–3 at halftime never became comfortable. Saffron could lose a possession, fall behind again and still produce a defensive sequence capable of changing the next several minutes.

Tare’s first recorded sack came on fourth-and-three in the opening quarter. Another followed on Mt. Silver’s next possession. Thorpe nevertheless completed a nineteen-yard touchdown throw short right to Lynch at 2:03. The Reds were finding scoring answers around the pressure, and Lynch was particularly useful: he caught all five of his targets for seventy-four yards and two touchdowns, while adding eighty rushing yards on ten carries.

body.alt: Art Shelgon, Shelgon number 65, with a recovered football on the turf.
body.caption: Art Shelgon recovered a second-quarter Saffron fumble.

body.text: Saffron’s first lost fumble followed a short completion to Emmitt Smoth. Cranidos recovered, and the Reds eventually added a thirty-yard Venutieri field goal. On Saffron’s next possession, Art Shelgon sacked Archam Manning on fourth-and-one. Thorpe then found Gyarzalez for an eleven-yard touchdown. The scoreboard reached 17–0, even though the visitors’ defensive front had already supplied reasons to expect a competitive game.

Another Saffron fumble, this time on a sack, gave Shelgon a recovery and Mt. Silver another opportunity. Venutieri made a forty-two-yard kick. Octillery answered with Saffron’s first points from thirty yards, but Venutieri added a thirty-one-yarder off the upright before halftime. A team capable of repeatedly getting to the opposing quarterback had surrendered twenty-three points because its own possessions kept handing the advantage back.

“I love the way they kept fighting,” Trent Scarboro said. “I’m responsible for getting us ready to keep the ball, too. Those things belong in the same conversation. You can be proud of a player and still tell him exactly what we have to fix.”
The comeback took two different forms

Dam Skattebo brought Saffron back into the game during the third quarter. He scored on runs up the middle from two and six yards, and the Psi Corps held Mt. Silver scoreless in the period. Skattebo finished with eighty-two yards on twelve carries and forty-six receiving yards. He gave Manning useful gains without requiring every answer to travel deep downfield.

The deficit was six entering the fourth quarter. Venutieri’s fifty-one-yard field goal extended it to nine, and then another turnover made the situation much worse. HeeDee Lamb fumbled the ensuing kickoff return, with Mt. Silver’s number 55 Medicham recovering. Ftzpatrik found Lynch short left for a nineteen-yard touchdown on the next offensive play. Saffron trailed 33–17 with less than five minutes left.

That sequence could have become the final explanation for the defeat: three lost fumbles against a team that did not lose one. Saffron instead made the Reds defend every remaining opportunity. Manning’s twenty-eight-yard touchdown pass deep right to Lamb at 2:26 cut the gap, and Skattebo’s successful two-point run made it 33–25. Lamb had answered his return mistake with a scoring catch, an important distinction for a coach who insists on asking players to make the next play.

Tare then sacked Ftzpatrik on consecutive snaps. The Reds punted after an incomplete third-down pass, and Manning took over with 1:48 left. He completed seven yards to Skattebo, nineteen to Lamb and twelve to Bysson Witten around one incompletion. Mothel Irving caught the next throw short left and scored from twenty yards. Smoth’s two-point run tied it at thirty-three.

Manning finished twenty-four of thirty-three for 299 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. Lamb caught five passes for exactly one hundred yards; Irving caught eight for ninety-nine. The comeback had become a demonstration of the receivers’ different contributions, with Manning distributing the ball quickly enough to retain a chance after every completion. Saffron’s sixteen fourth-quarter points came with genuine urgency rather than harmless late scoring.

body.alt: Crem Ftzpatrik, Alcremie number 12, holds a football in a stadium tunnel.
body.caption: Crem Ftzpatrik’s relief appearance helped Mt. Silver finish the win.

body.text: Seventy-five seconds were enough

Mt. Silver’s return put the ball at its own thirty-four. Ftzpatrik opened with an incompletion, then found Gyarzalez for eight yards. On third-and-two, he threw deep right to Jenings for seventeen. The next snap produced another seventeen-yard completion to Jenings, this one deep left. After an afternoon of sacks, the Reds had created two consecutive gains that let them finish on their own terms.

Jenings caught six passes for 138 yards. His eleven targets included several unsuccessful attempts, but the two late completions supplied thirty-four yards at precisely the point when Mt. Silver needed to avoid returning the ball. Lynch’s nine-yard run followed, then a kneel and Venutieri’s winning kick. The recorded squib return left Saffron no further offensive snap.

The decisive drive also gave the Reds useful evidence for next week’s preparation. Ftzpatrik had completed throws to three different receivers across his appearance, and the final possession asked him to recover from an opening incompletion. He did so without a turnover, preserving the chance to let the kicker finish.

Venutieri scored eighteen of the Reds’ thirty-six points: five field goals and three extra points. His kicks came from thirty, forty-two, thirty-one, fifty-one and thirty-three yards. That range of assignments matters. He rescued possessions that had stalled, extended the fourth-quarter lead and finally decided the game. Calling him the finishing touch would leave out much of the work.

Saffron outgained Mt. Silver 393–391 and produced eighteen first downs to fourteen. The Reds converted seven of fourteen third downs; the Psi Corps converted one of six. Neither side threw an interception. The three lost Saffron fumbles and Venutieri’s perfect kicking afternoon provide a better explanation for the final three-point difference than a general declaration that one offense dominated the other.

The next week now looks different for both clubs. Saffron, 11–3, hosts an 11–3 Blackthorn team coming off a twelve-point loss to Cinnabar. Mt. Silver visits that same Cinnabar side with Thorpe unavailable, while Foo Warner has a new two-week report and cornerback Ninjask has one. The injury record does not identify the precise play that hurt Thorpe; the nine sacks still give McLarren plenty of protection work to review before the next game.

McLarren could enjoy the result and still recognize the work ahead. “Apparently they wanted to make sure Adam stayed involved,” he said. “He did. Now we need the next quarterback ready, the people around him ready, and a better answer when somebody gets through. Cinnabar isn’t going to give us the week off because this one was exciting.”

art.alt: Adam Venutieri, Venusaur number 18, watches a kick toward the uprights.

articles.title: Four more for BeckhmJr, and one touchdown too many for Dorrill
articles.dek: Accel BeckhmJr gained 270 receiving yards in Mossdeep’s 51–7 win. The unbeaten Eclipse now welcome an 11–3 Sunyshore team.
articles.author: mara-voss

body.text: Michael Dorrill could cross punts off this week’s discussion. Mossdeep did not attempt one at Canalave. Dram Marino threw seven touchdown passes, Accel BeckhmJr caught four of them, and the Eclipse won 51–7 to reach 14–0. The coach still had a fourth-and-one touchdown allowed, a loose ball and a missed extra point available for the meeting. An unbeaten record has done very little to shorten his agenda.

“They had fourth-and-one and got into the end zone,” Dorrill said. “The score before the play does not change the assignment on the play. We’ll review the front, the fit and the finish. If you want a meeting where we only watch our touchdowns, you can hold that one after we win a championship.”

BeckhmJr supplied enough material for that hypothetical meeting to last a while. He caught ten passes on twelve targets for 270 yards, scoring from sixty-one, twenty-nine, six and twenty-one. Marino completed twenty of twenty-four throws for 386 yards and no interceptions. Mossdeep’s passing game required only twenty-four attempts to score seven times, with Ninjulio Jones, Gronkaludon and Shawn Mareman also reaching the end zone.

The Eclipse led 34–0 at halftime and 48–0 after three quarters. Canalave gained 334 total yards, enough to move the ball repeatedly, but missed two field goals and lost a fumble before finding its lone touchdown early in the fourth. Mossdeep’s 431 yards came with a much higher rate of successful finishes. The difference was visible well before the final score made it enormous.
BeckhmJr changed the length of the field

Mossdeep’s opening touchdown required seven plays and sixty-two yards. Mareman ran for five and eight yards, BeckhmJr caught a thirteen-yard pass, and Jones gained twenty-seven on a deep throw left before adding six on a run. Marino finished with a two-yard pass short left to Gronkaludon at 2:14 of the first quarter. Several players had already made the defense account for them before BeckhmJr supplied the afternoon’s longest touchdown.

That score came on Mossdeep’s next possession. Marino found BeckhmJr deep left for sixty-one yards at 5:53 of the second quarter, and the drive was over after one play. Canalave had just missed its second field-goal attempt. The Bulwark’s opportunity to answer a seven-point deficit had turned into another seven points for the visitors almost immediately.

body.alt: Dram Marino, Drampa number 12, prepares a pass in Mossdeep colors.
body.caption: Dram Marino threw seven touchdown passes against Canalave.

body.text: The next Mossdeep touchdown took four plays. Jones caught an eleven-yard pass, Mareman ran for three, and Gronkaludon added eight through the air. Marino then threw deep right to BeckhmJr for twenty-nine yards. The receiver had scored on opposite sides of the field in successive possessions, forcing Canalave to confront the same player through different throws rather than simply defend one repeated location.

BeckhmJr’s third score came from six yards, short left, with 1:18 left in the half. His fourth came deep right for twenty-one at 2:17 of the third quarter. He averaged twenty-seven yards per catch across the game. Even removing the sixty-one-yard touchdown leaves nine receptions for 209 yards, which is an awkward calculation for anyone hoping one isolated breakdown explains the afternoon.

“Ten catches sounds better when you remember the two I didn’t catch,” BeckhmJr said. “Coach will remember them. I thought I’d save him the trouble of looking them up.” Marino’s assessment was more deliberate: “The ball has to go where we have the answer. Accel gave us a lot of answers. The other guys finished theirs, too.”

Jones caught four passes for seventy-two yards, including a twenty-four-yard touchdown immediately after Canalave’s lost fumble. Gronkaludon caught all three of his targets for twenty-three yards. Mareman’s one reception went for a seven-yard touchdown. Lorenzo Steel and George Kipple each added a seven-yard catch. BeckhmJr commanded the headline because the production was extraordinary; the remaining completions explain why Canalave could not treat him as the entire offense.
Canalave moved the ball and left points behind

The Bulwark’s first two possessions ended in missed field goals after drives of fifty-one and forty-four yards. Those possessions prevented the opening quarter from looking like an uninterrupted Mossdeep procession. They also gave Canalave nothing on the scoreboard. When a defense faces an offense finishing possessions as quickly as the Eclipse did, empty trips become increasingly difficult to absorb.

Slowking completed sixteen of twenty-five passes for 241 yards. Grafaiai caught all five of his targets for 105, while Ariados caught all four for fifty. Seismitoad added twenty-seven receiving yards to eighty-one on twenty-two carries. Canalave found productive individual matchups and finished with fourteen first downs, one more than Mossdeep. It still needed repeated difficult conversions to turn that movement into points.

Joey Sporeter recovered the second-quarter fumble after a sack of Slowking. Marino’s touchdown pass to Jones came on the next offensive snap. Later, Sporeter and Derrat Brooks each received two sacks in the defensive box score. Canalave finished six of sixteen on third down and punted three times. The pressure helped terminate possessions even when the Bulwark had already found enough completions to move away from their own end.

body.alt: Joey Sporeter, Breloom number 98, secures a football on the turf.
body.caption: Joey Sporeter recovered Canalave’s second-quarter fumble.

body.text: The one successful scoring drive ended with Seismitoad’s one-yard run up the middle on fourth-and-one at 5:58 of the fourth quarter. It was a genuine conversion against a Mossdeep defense with every reason to preserve the shutout. Dorrill can review the responsibility without inventing an individual error the recorded play does not identify. The log establishes the run, the distance and the touchdown; assigning a particular defender’s missed responsibility requires more.

Mossdeep’s offense also had a loose-ball moment. The third-quarter log records a sack and fumble recovered by Mareman, allowing the Eclipse to retain possession. Marino subsequently found Mareman for the seven-yard touchdown on third-and-seven. The official box score charges Marino with one sack and Mossdeep with no fumbles lost. Mareman’s recovery preserved the scoring opportunity. Dorrill can review the loose ball and the successful response in the same possession, with a clear distinction between the mistake and the teammate’s useful recovery.
Sunyshore arrives with a different argument

Adam Vinathorn added a fifty-two-yard field goal in the fourth quarter and made six of seven extra points. Mossdeep’s running backs were not asked to reproduce Mareman’s hundred-yard performance against Petalburg. Mareman carried seven times for twenty-two yards, while Poury Holt gained eighteen on three attempts. Jones added nine rushing yards. The passing touchdowns determined the game before a large rushing workload became necessary.

The Eclipse have now scored 648 points and allowed 124 through fourteen games. Those totals establish how consistently they have separated from opponents, but the next visitor has a useful recent result of its own. Sunyshore beat Rustboro 41–7, with Myles Gabite running for 144 yards and 88 Special catching four touchdown passes. The Starseekers bring an 11–3 record and enough productive players to demand a more specific plan than admiration for Mossdeep’s latest margin.

Mossdeep’s injury report has improved in the secondary. Marshall Flock and Luvrelle Revis no longer have the positive recovery counters they carried in the previous issue. That change supports discussion of their availability status; it does not establish a starting assignment or an appearance against Canalave. Ninjaskamara still has one reported week remaining, and Richard Furman has two. The backfield and coverage decisions remain relevant to a matchup with two different Sunyshore scoring threats.

The next defensive review can also separate pressure from coverage. Canalave completed sixteen passes and gained more than three hundred total yards, yet scored once. Mossdeep can value the stops while examining the completions that made them necessary. That is a more useful assignment than treating a forty-four-point margin as a complete report.

Canalave, now 7–7, visits an 8–6 Rustboro team that also needs to repair a heavy defeat. For Mossdeep, the next objective is immediate and demanding: contain Gabite, limit the passing combinations and finish its own possessions. Dorrill has the evidence for praise and correction in the same file. Seven passing touchdowns earned the win. The conceded touchdown remains available for Monday’s discussion.

art.alt: Accel BeckhmJr, Accelgor number 11, sprints with the football in Mossdeep magenta and gold.

articles.title: 88 Special scores four; Sunyshore heads to Mossdeep
articles.dek: The Starseekers answered an early Rustboro touchdown with forty-one straight points, combining Myles Gabite’s 144 rushing yards with a four-score receiving afternoon.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Rustboro scored first at Sunyshore. That fact belongs near the beginning because almost everything that followed favored the Starseekers. Shawn Watzon found SEARED BITE for a twenty-yard touchdown, the Stone led 7–0, and the home offense had an early problem to solve. Sunyshore answered with forty-one consecutive points, four touchdown catches by 88 Special and a running performance that gives unbeaten Mossdeep plenty to examine before Week 16.

Myles Gabite rushed sixteen times for 144 yards and two touchdowns in the 41–7 victory. DeZhaun Watzon completed twenty-three of thirty passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns without an interception. All four scoring throws went to 88 Special, who caught six passes for seventy-seven yards. Sunyshore improved to 11–3. Rustboro fell to 8–6 with an offense that produced five first downs and converted one of eleven third-down attempts.

“People are going to watch us next week,” Karson Jones said. “Good. They should see a team that knows what it is doing. Today we went behind, kept working and gave them something worth watching. Now we have to prepare for a team that has beaten everybody it has played.”

The Starseekers gained 454 yards to Rustboro’s 163. They ran for 175 as a team and held the Stone to twenty-six. The numerical difference was large enough to cover several styles of victory, but Sunyshore’s specific combination matters: Gabite created gains on the ground, and the passing game repeatedly finished through the same receiver. Mossdeep will have to account for both without assuming that stopping one removes the other.
Rustboro’s promising start ended quickly

Shawn Watzon’s touchdown pass to SEARED BITE came at 4:49 of the opening quarter, deep left on second-and-thirteen. The throw gave the Stone an early reward for attacking downfield. SEARED BITE finished with four catches for fifty-four yards and the touchdown. Gibby Timmy also produced a fifty-four-yard reception, though his five targets yielded only that one catch.

Rustboro’s defense then sacked DeZhaun Watzon for eight yards, with Tyrantrum recording the play. There was a brief, plausible outline of a competitive afternoon: an early passing touchdown, an opposing quarterback pushed backward, and a Stone team capable of making Sunyshore work for its response. The rest of the quarter supplied a much less comfortable direction.

Gabite scored on a twenty-six-yard run up the middle at 1:25. The extra point tied the game. His eventual nine-yard rushing average came from a workload large enough to matter, rather than a single attempt displayed as a misleading rate. Sixteen carries gave Rustboro repeated opportunities to adjust, and Sunyshore continued to find productive runs.

body.alt: Jolt Vick, Jolteon number 24, catches a football near the sideline.
body.caption: Jolt Vick supplied six receptions for 87 yards.

body.text: The Stone never scored again. Philly carried fourteen times for thirty-one yards, with a long of seven. Shawn Watzon finished fifteen of twenty-five for 137 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. Avoiding interceptions preserved possessions, but too many of those possessions still ended before reaching a useful scoring position. Rustboro punted seven times and never attempted a field goal.

“You can have a very interesting first chapter and still turn in a book nobody wants to finish,” Tyler Scarboro said. “We scored. Then we kept giving the ball back. I don’t need a literary committee to explain one-for-eleven on third down.”
Four throws to number eighty-eight

Sunyshore took the lead on a ten-yard touchdown pass deep right to 88 Special at 3:52 of the second quarter. The same combination scored again from seventeen yards with forty-four seconds left in the half, this time on third-and-five. The Starseekers led 21–7 at the break, having made Rustboro defend both the run and a receiver who kept finishing the passing possessions.

The third touchdown catch came at 4:35 of the third quarter, on a twenty-five-yard throw deep left. Watzon returned to the left for an eight-yard score at 4:43 of the fourth. The four scoring passes traveled to both sides of the field and arrived from different distances. That variety is useful evidence for the coming matchup: Sunyshore did not need a single repeated throw to produce its largest receiving contribution.

88 Special’s six catches came on eight targets. Four ended in touchdowns; the other two contributed seventeen yards between them. It was an unusually concentrated scoring line, but the rest of the receiving group kept the offense from depending entirely on those finishes. Jolt Vick caught six passes for eighty-seven yards. Fera LaGatr caught six for seventy-six. MF STOMP caught all four of his targets for thirty-four.

“He put it where I could catch it,” 88 Special said. “I caught it. We can keep it that simple.” The quiet answer suited a receiver whose production already supplied most of the emphasis. Watzon’s explanation was less tidy: “Sometimes the best thing is to throw to the guy who just made you look clever. Then you have to make the right read again anyway.”

Sunyshore converted three of seven third downs. That figure is useful alongside the nineteen first downs: the offense often made progress without waiting for a difficult final attempt. Rustboro faced eleven third downs and converted one. The Stone repeatedly reached the point where the next snap had to preserve a possession, while Sunyshore found enough earlier gains to keep several possessions moving more freely.

body.alt: DeZhaun Watzon, Porygon-Z number 30, viewed from above on the field.
body.caption: DeZhaun Watzon completed 23 of 30 passes for 279 yards and four scores.

body.text: The defense kept the lead useful

Poliwrath sacked Shawn Watzon for eight yards on third-and-five in the second quarter. Later, Anorith ended a fourth-and-one attempt with a six-yard sack. Those were the two sacks charged to Rustboro’s quarterback, and both arrived on downs when a stop immediately affected possession. They were consequential interventions in a game that did not require a turnover to separate the teams.

Neither side threw an interception or lost a fumble. Sunyshore won through sustained production and stops rather than a succession of short-field gifts. Rustboro’s seven punts and limited rushing output demanded too much of a defense already trying to contain Gabite. The clearest summary remains the five first downs against nineteen.

Gabite added the final touchdown on a three-yard run up the middle on fourth-and-two with 1:20 left. The extra point missed, leaving the margin at thirty-four. His earlier twenty-six-yard touchdown had tied the game; this one completed a much longer stretch of Sunyshore control. The Starseekers had continued to use him in meaningful situations after the passing game had supplied most of the middle-period scoring.

Rustboro’s final possession included an eleven-yard completion to SEARED BITE, then ended when a three-yard pass to Geodude fell short on fourth-and-six. Sunyshore knelt twice to finish. That ending resembled too much of the Stone’s afternoon: a useful completion, another difficult down and insufficient distance when possession depended on it.
Two immediate tests

Sunyshore visits Mossdeep next, carrying eleven wins into a stadium where the opponent has fourteen and no losses. The Eclipse just won 51–7 at Canalave behind seven passing touchdowns. The Starseekers’ own four-touchdown receiver and 144-yard runner make this a much more substantial matchup than a simple comparison of the two latest margins. Both offenses have just demonstrated more than one way to reach the end zone.

The injury report still gives Serp Gardener one week, while Floatzel’s previous positive counter has cleared. A cleared designation does not promise a return to a particular role. Jones must prepare the available coverage group for Accel BeckhmJr, who gained 270 receiving yards at Canalave. The Starseekers’ offense can help by extending possessions, but it cannot assume Mossdeep will need many snaps to answer.

Rustboro hosts 7–7 Canalave, another team coming off a heavy defeat and another direct participant in the crowded playoff chase. My Way, Son still has three reported weeks remaining. Scarboro’s immediate task is to create more usable rushing situations and more successful passing downs with the players available. The early touchdown at Sunyshore showed that a scoring answer existed. The next game requires enough additional answers to keep the ball.
Jones will want the same patience if Mossdeep scores first. Sunyshore has just shown it can recover from an early deficit without abandoning its running game.

art.alt: 88 Special, Sceptile number 88, reaches for a touchdown reception in hot pink and black.

articles.title: Lavender holds on, then faces eight weeks without Mr. Clanky
articles.dek: Might Guy caught both Wails touchdowns in a 20–17 win over Celadon. A major new injury leaves Travis Scarboro preparing another quarterback plan.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Quilladin recovered the onside kick, Frosmoth knelt twice, and Lavender could finally put a 20–17 win over Celadon into the standings. The Wails had led 17–3 at halftime. With forty-eight seconds left, that advantage had shrunk to three points and the ball was available for another argument. Quilladin’s recovery prevented Celadon from making it.

Lavender improved to 9–5, but the news after the game was more difficult. Mr. Clanky, who completed six of eight passes for 121 yards, a touchdown and an interception, now has an eight-week injury report. Frosmoth completed thirteen of twenty-two for 163 yards and another touchdown. The precise injury play was not identified. Lavender still has the two passing performances to review, including the successful throws and the situations that forced a change of plan. That work becomes more important with Cerulean waiting on the schedule.

Might Guy caught five passes for 105 yards and both Lavender touchdowns. Just a cactus made field goals from forty-one and forty-four yards, plus both extra points. The Wails finished with 321 yards to Celadon’s 250, yet spent the last minute protecting a result that had appeared much more comfortable at halftime. Their ninth victory came with a new absence and several possessions worth reviewing.

“We won the game,” Travis Scarboro said. Asked about the quarterback situation, he was more expansive. “Two players threw passes. We’ll review both sets of snaps, work with the available players and prepare the next plan. The next opponent will have a defense. We should account for that.”
Might Guy supplied the scoring catches

Just a cactus opened the scoring with his forty-one-yard field goal at 2:44 of the first quarter. Mr. Clanky then found Might Guy short right for a four-yard touchdown with three seconds left in the period. The extra point made it 10–0. Lavender had created the early lead through two different finishes and had enough passing production to suggest more opportunities would follow.

Mr. Clanky’s second-quarter interception gave Celadon a chance to change the afternoon. Raboot took the deep-right throw and returned it fourteen yards. Clamperl subsequently made a thirty-seven-yard field goal, bringing the Bloom within seven. The Wails had given away a possession, and the visitors had converted the opportunity into points, even if they had not reached the end zone.

Lavender’s defense then supplied its own interception. With fifty-seven seconds left in the half, Doc Ock took Infernape’s short-middle pass. Frosmoth found Might Guy deep left for a fourteen-yard touchdown at 0:14, and the extra point sent the Wails into halftime ahead 17–3. A defensive intervention had become a touchdown before Celadon could get to the break.

body.alt: Doc Ock, Octillery number 97, holds a football in Lavender purple.
body.caption: Doc Ock’s interception helped Lavender protect its lead.

body.text: Might Guy’s longest catch went sixty yards. His five receptions came on ten targets, so the final line contained both a large contribution and several unsuccessful attempts. Wailord added five catches for seventy-four yards, Unfezant four for sixty-one, and Luvdisc four for thirty-three. Frosmoth and Mr. Clanky had enough receiving support to produce 284 passing yards between them.

“If it comes my way, I want it,” Might Guy said. “Both of them know that. I’m going to tell the next one, too, just so nobody gets confused.” His impatience to receive the ball was easier to indulge after two touchdowns. Scarboro’s interest will extend to the other five targets, the spacing around them and the situations the quarterbacks faced when those throws failed.
The rushing game left difficult work

Lavender ran eighteen times for thirty-seven yards. Mauler Twin gained ten on nine attempts. Machoke produced nineteen on five, and Mr. Clanky added ten on two before the kneels reduced Frosmoth’s rushing line. The Wails had to make their passing gains count because the running game supplied limited relief when a possession needed ordinary forward progress.

Frosmoth took two sacks, one from each of Celadon’s two Klawf defenders. The Wails converted four of ten third downs and punted three times. Those totals do not describe an offense that was unable to function; they describe one that still had several chances to make the afternoon easier and did not take all of them. The second half brought no Lavender touchdown.

Celadon’s offense had its own restrictions. Infernape finished fourteen of twenty-eight for 180 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Diggersby carried fourteen times for fifty-two yards. The Bloom converted two of eleven third downs and punted six times. For much of the game, Lavender’s defense stopped possessions before the visitors could fully exploit the opportunities their own defense created.

Ponyta caught four passes for eighty-seven yards, giving Celadon its largest receiving contribution. Carnivine caught two of eight targets for twenty-one. The difference between those lines helps explain why a few good gains did not become a steady scoring afternoon. Infernape had useful answers, but the Bloom repeatedly needed another one on the next difficult down.
The return fumble reopened the game

At the start of the fourth quarter, Mimikyu returned a punt twenty-two yards and fumbled. Celadon’s Diggersby recovered. Infernape eventually finished the opportunity with a one-yard touchdown pass short left to number 66 Wobbuffet at 3:56. The missed extra point left the score 17–9, preserving an eight-point gap rather than reducing it to seven.

body.alt: Frosmoth number 15 watches the field beside a football.
body.caption: Frosmoth threw for 163 yards and a touchdown in relief.

body.text: That mistake made Lavender’s next scoring possession particularly important. Near the two-minute warning, Rhyperior ran for two yards and Machoke for seven. Machoke then gained nothing on third-and-one. Just a cactus made a forty-four-yard field goal off the upright at 1:53. The Wails had missed the first down they wanted, but the kick forced Celadon to find more than one ordinary touchdown to complete the comeback.

Celadon responded with its best late sequence. After two incompletions, Infernape found Houndoom for eight. On fourth-and-two, he completed a twenty-four-yard pass deep right to Ponyta. Diggersby followed with a twenty-seven-yard catch, and Wobbuffet gained fifteen on the next completion. Deerling’s three-yard touchdown run left fifty-one seconds on the clock.

Infernape completed the two-point try to Wobbuffet, making it 20–17. The visitors had turned a stalled-looking possession into seventy-eight yards and a touchdown, using a fourth-down conversion to keep the attempt alive. Lavender’s defense had done enough earlier to protect a lead; this sequence showed why that work still needed a secure finish from the return team.

Quilladin recovered the onside kick at Celadon’s forty-five. Frosmoth’s kneels completed the game. The recovery will not dominate a receiver’s highlight reel or a quarterback’s statistical line, but it ended the last practical route Celadon had to change the result. In a three-point game, securing that ball was a complete assignment.
A road trip with a changed plan

Lavender now visits 7–7 Cerulean. The Tide won 20–17 at Azalea and remain involved in the same conference’s crowded race. The Wails’ 9–5 record gives them a useful advantage, but the new eight-week absence means their preparation must begin with available personnel rather than the assumption that the same passing combination can simply be repeated.

Frosmoth has recent evidence to work from: thirteen completions, 163 yards and a touchdown in this game, plus his earlier relief work. That is a practical starting point for the staff. It does not make every future possession predictable or excuse the weak rushing output. People Eater still has two reported weeks remaining, leaving another established receiving absence on the preparation sheet.

Mr. Clanky is listed at SLOT in the current roster information, yet his passing contribution here is directly recorded. The distinction matters for describing the injury accurately: Lavender has lost a player who just handled meaningful quarterback work, whatever label appears beside his name. Scarboro must replace the actual job performed on the field. His next plan will be judged by the available players’ work at Cerulean, after a week in which the Wails secured the win and learned how much preparation still lay ahead.
The next practice gives Scarboro a chance to establish that passing rhythm before another close finish makes every incomplete throw more expensive.

articles.title: Cinnabar finishes four passing touchdowns at Blackthorn
articles.dek: Gholdengo spread the scores among four receivers as the Blaze won 31–19, reached 9–5 and secured their division. Mt. Silver comes next.
articles.author: dorian-pike

body.text: Blaine, that is a much better time to start scoring touchdowns. Cinnabar went to Blackthorn, produced two touchdown drives in the second quarter and added another in each quarter after halftime. Gholdengo threw four scoring passes to four different receivers. The Blaze won 31–19, improved to 9–5 and secured Kanto West. A team that had recently needed a lecture about starting its comeback earlier spent this afternoon making the opponent chase.

Gholdengo finished twenty of thirty-four for 323 yards and no interceptions. Arcanine caught six passes for 138 yards and a touchdown. Archaludon, Wigglytuff and the receiver recorded in the play log as Frogadier supplied the other scoring catches. That last player has since evolved from Frogadier to Greninja. His five catches and seventy-seven yards supplied another receiving contribution alongside Arcanine’s larger total, and his scoring play gave the Blaze an eighteen-point fourth-quarter lead.

Blackthorn fell to 11–3 after a second straight loss. The Dragons had scored three points at Lavender in Week 14 and managed nineteen here. Hatterene completed twenty-five of thirty-three passes for 261 yards and two touchdowns, but Blackthorn lost two fumbles and ran for thirty-seven yards. Cinnabar did not need an interception to take possessions away or to make its passing production decisive.

“We gave ourselves chances and finished enough of them,” Blaine said. “There are still possessions we want back. Against that team, you have to keep playing after a good series.” The upcoming opponent makes that last sentence useful. Mt. Silver visits next at 13–1, carrying a three-point win over Saffron and a major new quarterback injury.
The opening mistakes did not last all afternoon

Cinnabar’s first possession included consecutive sacks of Gholdengo on second-and-ten and third-and-seventeen. Lucario took him down for seven yards, and Sharpedo followed for six. The Blaze punted. Anyone prepared to explain the entire game through that opening sequence would have been busy revising the explanation by halftime.

Blackthorn took a 3–0 lead on Cacturne’s twenty-seven-yard field goal. Charjabug answered from forty-three. Then Sawsbuck fumbled a six-yard run, and Escavalier recovered for Cinnabar. The Blaze did not immediately turn that takeaway into points: Vigoroth sacked Gholdengo on fourth-and-two. Blackthorn had defended one dangerous opportunity and kept the game level.

The next turnover was more expensive. Hatterene fumbled on a second-quarter sack, with Cinnabar’s Gumshoos recovering. Gholdengo found Archaludon short left for a thirteen-yard touchdown on third-and-seven at 4:36. The extra point made it 10–3. This time the Blaze had taken the extra possession and supplied the finish it required.

body.alt: Archaludon number 78 holds a touchdown reception near the goal line.
body.caption: Archaludon caught a 13-yard second-quarter touchdown.

body.text: That distinction deserves attention because teams are often credited with an entire game’s competence after one recovery. Cinnabar wasted one short opportunity and used the next. The winning performance contained both. The useful correction for Blaine is to preserve the successful response without forgetting the failed fourth-down protection that preceded it.

Gholdengo’s boldness had support from the receivers. Archaludon caught four of five targets for fifty yards. Wigglytuff had only one reception, but it was an eight-yard touchdown on fourth-and-six at 1:53 of the second quarter. The Blaze led 17–3 before Blackthorn added a thirty-two-yard field goal near halftime. Cinnabar had made a fourth-down passing decision produce the touchdown that its earlier fourth-down attempt had failed to deliver.
Four receivers finished four different possessions

Blackthorn reduced the deficit to 17–13 on a two-yard Hatterene touchdown pass to Seadra in the third quarter. The Dragons had a chance to make the afternoon uncomfortable. Cinnabar answered with a sixteen-yard touchdown pass deep right to Arcanine on third-and-nine at 0:29. The Blaze restored an eleven-point lead before the quarter ended.

Arcanine’s 138 receiving yards came on nine targets. His longest catch went thirty-five yards, and his six completions gave Gholdengo useful production beyond the scoring play. The receiver’s restrained response was appropriate to the line: “I had room on some of them. I wanted to make sure the catch came first.” Cinnabar benefited every time that modest description turned into another substantial gain.

The fourth touchdown pass went short left for nine yards on third-and-three at 3:31 of the fourth quarter. The game log names Frogadier; the postgame box page now displays Greninja for that same player. His five catches produced seventy-seven yards, including a fifty-five-yard gain. That combination of a long reception and a shorter scoring finish gave Cinnabar another useful route through the defense.

Gholdengo’s four scoring throws came on third-and-seven, fourth-and-six, third-and-nine and third-and-three. Those are unusually clear receipts for an offense asked to make consequential passing downs work. The Blaze converted six of ten third downs overall. They did not reach every score through an easy sequence of first-down runs or rely on one receiver to rescue every stalled possession.

“If we have the throw, I want to make it,” Gholdengo said. “The down matters because we need the yards. It doesn’t change whether the receiver is there.” That confidence worked here because four different players completed the assignment at the end of the pass. It will need the same support against Mt. Silver’s defense.

body.alt: Pidgeotto number 11 carries the football across open turf.
body.caption: Pidgeotto’s late runs helped Cinnabar close out the victory.

body.text: Blackthorn found completions without control

Hatterene’s twenty-five completions should prevent anyone from describing the Dragons’ offense as incapable of moving the ball. Exploud caught six passes for seventy-four yards. Tinkaton caught six for fifty-one and a touchdown. Seadra caught all four of his targets for thirty-four and a score. Blackthorn gained thirteen first downs, only one fewer than Cinnabar.

The Dragons’ rushing game gave those completions limited assistance. Sawsbuck carried seven times for seventeen yards, Gumshoos twice for eleven and Mudbray three times for nine. The total was thirty-seven yards on twelve attempts. Blackthorn had to continue finding passing answers while Cinnabar accumulated the advantage from its own scoring drives and the two recovered fumbles.

Hatterene’s late five-yard touchdown pass to Tinkaton brought the score to 31–19 with 1:57 left. Cacturne missed the extra point. Buizel then recovered the onside kick for Cinnabar at midfield. Blackthorn had produced another scoring possession, but the failed recovery left the Dragons needing stops and time they did not have.

Pidgeotto ran for nine and thirteen yards on the next two plays. Gholdengo knelt twice. Those twenty-two rushing yards came when the Blaze needed to remove Blackthorn’s remaining opportunity, and they supplied an efficient finish to a game otherwise led by the passing attack. Pidgeotto ended with twenty-five yards on three carries. The final two attempts mattered considerably more than their share of the afternoon’s headlines.
The next opponent makes the preparation obvious

Cinnabar finished with 397 total yards, one punt and no turnovers. Charjabug made the one field-goal attempt and all four extra points. The Blaze had enough production in several areas to withstand the three sacks charged to Gholdengo and the failed early fourth-down attempt. That combination gives Blaine specific work to preserve before the schedule becomes difficult again.

The injury report introduces a new concern at halfback. Seismitoad has a two-week report after contributing sixteen yards on four carries. Octillery, the outside linebacker, still has three weeks remaining from an earlier injury. Cinnabar cannot assume its full preferred personnel will be available simply because the division title is secured. Its next offensive plan has to account for the actual absence and the other backs’ demonstrated contributions.

Blackthorn visits 11–3 Saffron, whose defense recorded nine sacks at Mt. Silver despite losing 36–33. Grovyle still has one reported week remaining. The Dragons have now encountered consecutive opponents that prevented their season record from settling the game in advance. Protection, ball security and more useful rushing possessions are concrete subjects for Clair’s preparation.

For Cinnabar, Mt. Silver offers a chance to test this passing performance against another leading club immediately. The Reds will be preparing around Tic Thorpe’s new six-week absence, but their winning drive against Saffron showed that another passer can still find Gregar Jenings and arrange a decisive kick. Blaine has earned the division. Next week asks whether four-touchdown football can survive another demanding opponent.
